messages:
Jon: Heads-up — seeing a sharp tail-latency increase in eu-west dedicated pools around 03:10 UTC. 95th/99th up ~3-4x. Correlates with a single tenant (t-742) egress spike and repeated KV cache regen logs.

Jon: snippet from logs:
```
[03:09:58] kvcache: eviction-iter 42 tenant=t-742 reclaimed=0 miss_rate=0.87
[03:10:02] net: egress tx=5.8Gbps pcie-inflight=180ms queue=99%
[03:10:05] gpu0: stall-detect seq=17 -> latency spike
```

Infra-bot: Alert: eu-west-pool-23 tail_latency_99 > 600ms for 3m; triggered by tenant t-742. IncidentID: inc-2026-1007-eu23

Areesa: Is t-742 on a dedicated slice or shared? any recent deploys?

Jon: t-742 is on a fractional-dedicated slice (reserved) — popped a big batch job this morning (unknown new commit). No deploys from our side observed in the last hour.

Maria: Quick mitigation options: 1) apply egress policer to t-742 (1Gbps) 2) temporarily route t-742 to an ephemeral spillover pool (ephemeral-eu-west-hot) 3) enable kvcache-protect flag for pool to avoid aggressive eviction. Easiest low-risk: egress cap + enable kvcache-protect.

Maria: router command (canary):
```
routerctl set-policy --tenant t-742 --egress-cap 1gbps --comment "temp cap due noisy-neighbor"
routerctl route --tenant t-742 --target pool:ephemeral-eu-west-hot --mode drain-if-needed
```

Kevin: FYI cost / product note — moving to ephemeral or warm-hot slices increases per-token infra cost (hot slice is ~2.2x host rate). If we keep the egress cap long, tenants may fail large batched jobs. Need quick estimate on incremental cost before we move.

Maria: rough back-of-envelope: if t-742 keeps 5.8Gbps -> capping to 1Gbps reduces egress bill ~80% for that tenant but could extend runtime 4-6x -> compute cost maybe +10-15% for the slice depending on GPU time. Moving to ephemeral hot pool for 30m ~= $120 extra (ballpark).

sre-oncall: Playbook snippet to run now:
1) apply egress cap 1Gbps (routerctl)
2) enable kvcache-protect on pool (feature flag)
3) watch tail latency and pcie stalls for 10m
4) if tail persists -> route tenant to spillover and notify customer success

sre-oncall: Commands:
```bash
# apply cap
routerctl set-policy --tenant t-742 --egress-cap 1gbps
# soft-enable kvcache protection
fleetctl annotate pool eu-west-pool-23 kvcache-protect=true
```

Areesa: Can someone grab the tenant owner (eng team) and ping them? I can open a quick customer notif if we plan to reroute.

Jon: I'm on it — DMing owner now. Applying egress cap in 30s.

Jon: applied cap. monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/re/cluster/eu-west/pool-23 (watching 99th).

Maria: thanks — I'll prepare the ephemeral route in case drain needed.

Kevin: pls post cost delta if we route them to ephemeral. Ops will need to sign off if >$200 for the next hour.

Jon: 10m in: tail 99p down from 620ms -> 220ms, egress for t-742 down to ~0.9Gbps. pcie stalls drop. Looks like cap helped.

Areesa: nice. keep it for now and escalate to product if they complain about slow batch runs.

Infra-bot: Resolve suggestion: Monitor 30m; auto-unwind cap if tenant drops below 200Mbps for 10m.

Jon: noted. I'll leave cap and kvcache-protect for 30m and then re-evaluate. :thumbsup:
